brief: A closed electronics enclosure with a louvred vent so the board inside can breathe.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases (0,0,0; 1,0,0; 0,1,0) joined by joint bolts, a solid top and bottom cover on each cell, and all 12 exposed side faces closed with caps. Last check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Louvred vent so the board inside can breathe
requirements.evidence: The top cover over cell 1,0,0 is set to the grate cover type, the closest available vent style to a louvre. It is a vent in the top face only. I did not verify louvre geometry visually, and no board was placed inside, so airflow to a specific board is not confirmed.

finish.summary: Built a closed three-cell hex enclosure (all faces covered or capped; check_build clean, meshClash clear) with a grate-type vent on the top of one cell. The grate is the nearest available vent style to a louvre, and I did not add an internal board or tray, so fit of a board inside is unverified.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
